correctness.rationale: All 144 branch matrices are explicitly enumerated with exact Fraction arithmetic; step decomposition bounds each stochastic matrix on path variation. Exactly one mask, (3,0,0,3), has a coefficient exceeding 11/6, equal to 2. Comparing full-ball and three-ball endpoint averages and the middle singleton/full averages proves this mask can be active only for constant inputs. Integrating piecewise-affine derivatives along arbitrary nonnegative input segments proves a universal bound. The explicit positive pair gives equality, with no limiting argument; tests confirm the rational certificate but are not substituted for the continuous proof.

value.rationale: P4 is the first non-star unweighted path and the first diameter-three tree path, so its exact two-input maximal-variation gain is a natural minimal structural benchmark. The 11/6 factor contrasts sharply with known one-input variation behavior and demonstrates the necessity of excluding algebraically feasible but dynamically inactive branch-matrix norms. This resolves a meaningful graph-maximal perturbation stability question exactly, rather than an arbitrary parameter table.
